official.deadline_note: Applications for the Class of 2028 open on Tuesday, 9 March 2027 and close by the end of Wednesday, 14 April 2027 at 23:59 GMT+2; no late or incomplete applications will be accepted under any circumstances. Applications for 2027 are now closed.
official.application_cycle: Class of 2028 (annual cycle running March to November for the following year's intake)
official.status_note: The Foundation states 'Applications for 2027 are now closed' and 'Applications for 2028 will open 9 March 2027'; as of the verification date the next round has not yet opened.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published: 'The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship offers comprehensive funding for the core costs associated with your studies. It covers tuition for a one-year Honours degree or a two-year Masters degree in any field at a recognised South African institution of higher education. This includes tuition and registration fees, allowances for study materials, research, and medical aid, accommodation and meals, personal allowance and economy class travel to and from your home country to your South African university at the beginning and end of your degree.'
benefits: Tuition and registration fees as set by your university or institution
A study materials allowance as set by the MRF
Accommodation and meal allowances as set by the MRF
A medical aid allowance as set by the MRF
A personal allowance as set by the MRF
Research and conferencing grants can be made available on request
Economy-class flights for international scholars from their home countries to their institutions at the start and end of their studies
eligibility: I can study at a postgraduate level in English
I am a citizen of an African country
I am between the ages of 19 and 29 in the year of applying (under 30 at the time of taking up the scholarship)
By 1 Jan 2028, I will have an undergraduate degree with excellent academic results (above 70% or upper-second class Honours)
I aspire to be an ethical leader and I am committed to using my talents to advance equality, freedom and human dignity in Africa
I am prepared to reflect deeply on my own leadership and undergo a process of personal change and growth
requirements: Apply online through the Foundation's applications platform
Three letters of recommendation, in English, submitted by the recommenders directly through the application platform
Upload certificates of completion for your degrees, transcripts of your academic results (in English), and scans of your ID and passport documents
Write two short essays: one on your personal journey, and one on a specific question relating to the Foundation's principles
State your proposed course of study; proof of having applied to a university is not required but is highly recommended
documents: Three letters of recommendation in English, uploaded by the recommenders on the platform
Certificates of completion for your degrees
Transcripts of your academic results, in English
Scans of your ID and passport documents
Two short essays (personal journey, and a question on the Foundation's principles)
selection_criteria: Leadership: aspiring to visionary leadership with moral authority and the advancement of equality, freedom, human rights and human dignity
Reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship: excellent academic results paired with character, and demonstrated individual effort, innovation and creativity

Round-based screening: notification by mid-July for Round Two, by end of July for Round Three, by end of August for the Final Round interview, with interviews in South Africa in October and selection notified by end of October
coverage: Tuition and registration fees as set by your university or institution
Study materials, accommodation and meal, medical aid and personal allowances as set by the MRF
Research and conferencing grants, available on request
Economy-class flights for international scholars at the start and end of their studies
application_method: Register on the Foundation's applications platform once applications open on 9 March 2027
Add three recommenders on the platform before the close
Upload certificates, transcripts, ID and passport scans and both essays
Have the three recommenders sign in to the platform and upload their English letters
Submit the complete application before 14 April 2027, 23:59 GMT+2
official.application_route: Online application on the Mandela Rhodes Foundation's platform; the three recommenders upload their letters on the same platform before the deadline.
official.study_mode: In-person study at a South African institution - distance learning is not allowed, so that scholars can participate in the leadership development programme.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of an African country, wherever currently living or studying; the degree must be undertaken at a South African institution.
official.international_eligibility: Open to citizens of any African country, including those living and studying outside Africa; study must take place in South Africa and cannot be undertaken in the scholar's home country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Honours and Masters degrees in any field at a recognised South African institution; the Foundation does not fund MBAs, any type of block course, or courses delivered predominantly online.
official.duration: One year of funding for an Honours degree and one or two years for a Masters, to a strict maximum of two years with no exceptions.
official.description: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship combines financial support with a leadership programme built on the founding principles of reconciliation, education, entrepreneurship and leadership, challenging scholars to grow and connecting them to young African changemakers. It offers comprehensive funding for the core costs of a one-year Honours or two-year Masters degree at a recognised South African institution.
official.program_type: Foundation postgraduate scholarship with leadership development programme
official.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to do written and verbal academic work in English at a postgraduate level; English is the main medium of tuition at South African universities. The Foundation offers a free self-test and publishes no required IELTS or TOEFL score.

verification.notes: Read the Mandela Rhodes Foundation's own apply page and its funding, visa, application and timeline FAQs in full on 2026-10-10; the coverage list, eligibility requirements, Class of 2028 dates, selection rounds and conditions of tenure are confirmed as published. The Foundation publishes no monetary value for any allowance.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no published rand figure: the Foundation pays tuition and registration directly to your university and pays all other allowances to you twice a year, so your planning has to anchor on your institution's real fee statement. Winning depends as much on the two essays, the three referee letters and the leadership interview as on marks. The award cannot be deferred, you may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities, paid work is capped at 12 hours a week, and the compulsory residential workshops are a condition of the scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African citizens aged 19-29 with an above-70% or upper-second undergraduate record who intend to study an Honours or Masters in South Africa and will commit to the compulsory residential leadership programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm citizenship, age (19-29 in the year of applying) and that your undergraduate degree will be complete by 1 January 2028
Approach three recommenders before applications open on 9 March 2027 and give them time to upload letters on the platform
Prepare degree certificates, English transcripts and ID/passport scans in advance
Draft both essays against the Foundation's principles - one on your personal journey, one on the published principles question
Apply to South African universities in parallel, to more than one institution, because the award is conditional on a place
For qualifications from outside South Africa, start SAQA verification early - it takes 4-8 weeks and is not covered
common_rejection_risks: Recommender letters missing at the deadline - the application cannot be submitted or considered without them
Essays that ignore the principles question or read as generic leadership statements
No South African university place by January of the year of residence, which makes the award impossible to accept
Transcripts or documents not in English
Turning 30 before taking up the scholarship, or applying for an MBA, block course or online programme that is not funded
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: University application fees, SAQA verification of prior degrees and visa application costs are explicitly not covered; any amount owed before becoming a Scholar is the scholar's sole responsibility, and passports or travel documents for shortlisted interviewees are not paid for.
document_audit: All documents and transcripts must be provided in English
Recommenders upload their letters themselves on the platform - letters sent by email do not count
Certificates of completion are required, not just enrolment or provisional results
alerts: Applications for the current cycle are closed; the Class of 2028 window is only 9 March to 14 April 2027
The scholarship cannot be deferred and must be accepted for the year it is offered
Travel outside South Africa, even for research, is not accepted as a reason for missing compulsory programme activities
You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities, and paid work is limited to 12 hours per week
SAQA verification can take 4-8 weeks and can delay both university acceptance and the study visa
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the MRF platform when applications open, upload documents and essays, have three recommenders upload letters, and submit by 14 April 2027; staged rounds run July to October with final-round interviews in South Africa and selection notified by end of October.
